# muxt reads templates with {{ and }}. A set built with Delims is not
# supported, and this pins what a project using one is told.
#
# The define clause is written in the set's own delimiters, so muxt does not
# see a definition named "greeting" at all and cannot connect the
# ExecuteTemplate call to a template. It says so and exits non-zero.
#
# What matters is that it is loud. A tool that reported "0 mutants, 0 missed"
# here would read as a clean bill of health for templates it never read.

! muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1
cmpenv stderr want-err.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
[[define "greeting"]]Hello, [[.Name]]![[if .Loud]] !!![[end]][[end]]
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.New("t").Delims("[[", "]]").ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Greeting struct {
	Name string
	Loud bool
}

func Render(w io.Writer, greeting Greeting) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", greeting)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreeting(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Greeting{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want-err.txt --
Error: no templates.ExecuteTemplate calls found: mutation testing needs a call site to know the type of dot
